title: Spelling
about: Greek writes the sound [i] six ways and [o] two ways, and the spelling carries grammar: *-ει* is a verb ending, *-η* a feminine noun ending, *-οι* a masculine plural, *-εται* a passive third person singular, *-ετε* an active second person plural. Most spelling mistakes are really grammar mistakes, so ask which form you need before you ask how it is spelled.

items.en: Nikos is coming from Larissa tomorrow.

errs.why: Third person singular of verbs in *-ομαι* ends in *-εται*: *έρχεται*, *κάθεται*, *λέγεται*. *-ετε* is the active "you (plural)": *έρχεστε*, *γράφετε*.

items.en: My friends live in Germany.

errs.why: Masculine plural in *-οι*: *οι φίλοι*, *οι δρόμοι*. *-ει* is a verb ending.

items.en: On Saturday we're going to the village.

errs.why: *Σάββατο* is spelled with double *β*. So are *Σαββατοκύριακο* and *Σάββας*.

items.en: Thank you very much for the help!

errs.why: Verbs end in *-ω*: *ευχαριστώ*, *μπορώ*, *γράφω*. Nouns in *-ο* are neuter: *το βιβλίο*.

parts: ωραίο είναι το καινούργιο σου σπίτι!
items.en: Your new house is nicer!

errs.why: *πιο* "more" (*πιο ωραίο*) and *ποιο* "which" (*ποιο σπίτι;*) sound the same. Here it means "more": *πιο ωραίο* "nicer".

parts: Ποιος είναι πιο ψηλός, ο Γιάννης ή ο Πέτρος;
items.en: Who's taller, Giannis or Petros?
items.why: Nothing to fix: *ποιος* "who/which" and *πιο* "more" are both right where they stand.

items.en: Yesterday I got lost in the alleys of Plaka.

errs.why: Passive aorists end in *-ηκα*: *χάθηκα*, *γεννήθηκα*, *κοιμήθηκα*.

items.en: Take whatever you want from the fridge.

errs.why: *ό,τι* (with a comma) means "whatever"; *ότι* means "that".

items.en: The solution to the problem was simple.

errs.why: Nouns in *-η* (feminine): *η λύση*, *η άσκηση*. *-ει* is the verb ending: *θα λύσει*.

items.en: I want you to come early.

errs.why: In today's spelling the subjunctive has the same endings as the present: *να έρθεις*, *να γράψει*. The old *-ης/-η* endings are no longer used.

items.en: The new phone is better than the old one.

errs.why: *καλύτερος* is written with *υ*.

items.en: Mykonos is nicer in May.

errs.why: The comparative suffix is *-ότερος* with omicron: *ωραιότερος*, *μικρότερος*. The *-ώτερος* spelling is old.

items.en: She ran off to catch the train.

errs.why: Gerunds end in *-οντας* or, when stressed, *-ώντας*: *τρέχοντας*, *γράφοντας*, but *μιλώντας*, *ρωτώντας*.

parts: Κάθεται όλη μέρα στο μπαλκόνι και διαβάζει.
items.en: He sits on the balcony all day reading.
items.why: Nothing to fix: *κάθεται* (*-εται*, passive form) and *διαβάζει* (*-ει*, active).

items.en: The European Union has 27 member states.

errs.why: When *α* and *ι* are pronounced separately and the *ι* is not stressed, the *ι* takes a diaeresis: *ευρωπαϊκός*, *αρχαϊκός*, *Πειραϊκός*.

items.en: The flight was delayed because of the strike.

errs.why: *εξαιτίας* is one word, with no apostrophe.

items.en: Besides, we didn't have time for everything.

errs.why: *εξάλλου* "besides" is written as one word.

items.en: Einstein was a great scientist.

errs.why: *ο επιστήμονας* is written with omicron: *επιστήμονας*, *των επιστημόνων*.

items.en: We bought a new bed for the children's room.

errs.why: Today's spelling is *κρεβάτι* with one *β*; *κρεββάτι* is the older spelling.

parts: Ούτως ή άλλως θα περάσουμε από το σπίτι σου.
items.en: We'll be passing by your house anyway.
items.why: Nothing to fix: *ούτως ή άλλως* "anyway" is written as three words, with *ή* "or" in the middle.

items.en: We found it in an old encyclopedia.

errs.why: *εγκυκλοπαίδεια* keeps *αι* from *παιδεία* "education".

items.en: His proposal was undoubtedly the best.

errs.why: Verbal adjectives in *-τος* keep the vowel the verb has in its aorist: *αμφισβήτησα* → *αναμφισβήτητος*, *κατανόησα* → *ακατανόητος*, *σημείωσα* → *αξιοσημείωτος*.

items.en: The town council expressed its solidarity with those affected.

errs.why: *αλληλεγγύη* is written with *γγ*, like *εγγύηση* and *εγγονός*.

items.en: The company lost two million euros.

errs.why: *εκατομμύριο* has double *μ*.

parts: τον ανάγκασε να σταματήσει να δουλεύει.
items.en: The chronic illness forced him to stop working.

errs.why: *η ασθένεια* is written with *-εια*, like *η αλήθεια*, *η συνήθεια*, *η βοήθεια*.

items.en: My worst habit is that I'm late everywhere.

errs.why: *η συνήθεια* ends in *-εια*. Its stress is on the third-last syllable, so before *μου* it also takes a second accent: *η συνήθειά μου*.

items.en: We laughed throughout the film.

errs.why: *καθ' όλη τη διάρκεια* "throughout" is two words: *καθ'* (= *κατά*) + *όλη*. *Καθόλου* "at all" is a different word.

parts: Η εκκλησία ήταν γεμάτη, αν και ήταν καθημερινή.
items.en: The church was full, even though it was a weekday.
items.why: Nothing to fix: *εκκλησία* with double *κ*, and *καθημερινή* "weekday" with *η* and *ι*.
